content.text: The text reviews diseases of the intestine, rectum, and anus, emphasizing typhlitis, intestinal ulcers, hemorrhage, obstruction, cancer, amyloid degeneration, and congenital malformations. It describes causes, anatomy, symptoms, complications, diagnosis, prognosis, and historical treatments, including opium, irrigation, diet, cold, enemas, aspiration, incision, laparotomy, colotomy, and rectal surgery. Major dangers include perforation, peritonitis, gangrene, hemorrhage, fistula, stricture, and fatal obstruction. Rectal disorders discussed include prolapse, polyps, hemorrhoids, fissures, ulcers, abscesses, fistulas, syphilis, tuberculosis, cancer, impaction, and neurologic dysfunction. John journeyed to the hallway.
